unverifiable_kinds: semantic or paraphrase equivalence of a checkpoint answer
behavioural claims requiring code execution ('function returns None', 'tests pass')
prose repair targets with no literal corrected value
prose negative constraints with no literal and no pinned path
constraint regex that does not compile

exit_codes.0: verified success: every required check passed and the fixture digest matched
exit_codes.1: not verified: a required check failed or was unverifiable, or the digest was not recorded
exit_codes.2: tampered: fixture sha256 at score time differs from the run-start digest
exit_codes.3: invalid input, stub/incomplete fixture, or no scoreable checks

assumptions: The longrun tree contained only stub fixtures ('stub': true) when this unit ran, so the scorer was aligned to the fixture shape documented in card 2a6c4761's prompt: task_id, class, objective, sources, turns, checkpoints[{turn,question,expected}], repair{at_turn,wrong_assumption,correct_action}, acceptance{checks,negative_constraints}, expected.
Run log may be NDJSON or one JSON document; the run-start fixture digest is read from fixture_sha256 / fixture_sha / fixture_digest on the header or any record.
A checkpoint answer is exact-match by default because the programme's preregistration uses exact match; fixtures may opt into contains/regex.
Exit 2 is reserved for tampering; usage/input errors use 3 so a script cannot confuse a bad fixture with a dishonest run.
